about.title: Albany Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Albany is a small, walkable city wedged between the I-80 corridor and San Pablo Avenue, and its residents rely daily on cars, household goods, tools, and consumer products bought locally or ordered online. When one of those products fails — a car part malfunctions on I-80, a kitchen appliance sparks a fire, a piece of exercise equipment collapses — the injuries can be sudden and serious. California law allows people hurt by defective products to pursue claims against manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers, often without having to prove anyone was careless. If you were hurt by a product in Albany, keeping the item exactly as it was at the time of the incident matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; instead, we connect Albany residents with independent attorneys who evaluate these cases and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Albany Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California often allows product liability claims under strict liability, meaning you may not need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer that sold the product can potentially be held liable, which widens the pool of parties an attorney may pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early On
items.desc: Because these claims often hinge on the physical evidence itself, an attorney can advise you on how to properly store the product so it isn't lost, altered, or discarded before it can be examined.

items.question: I was hurt by a product I bought online — does that change anything?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law generally allows claims against manufacturers, distributors, and sellers regardless of whether the purchase happened online or in a store. An attorney can help sort out which parties in the supply chain may be responsible.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Often no — California frequently applies strict liability to defective product cases, which means the focus is usually on whether the product was defective and caused harm, not on the manufacturer's state of mind. This can make these claims more approachable than some other injury cases.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me here in Albany?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, without repairing or discarding it. Given how many Albany residents travel the I-80 and San Pablo corridors and rely on everyday consumer goods, an attorney can advise on safe storage and next steps specific to your situation.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and the attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
